hand.pickChowFirst: Tap any tile of the run.
hand.pickChowMore: Tap {n} more — only tiles that fit are live.
hand.concealedKongFound: Four {tile} — counted as a concealed kong, so the hand is one tile longer.
flag.robbingKong.sub: You took the tile off someone adding it to their pong.
flag.robbingKong.detail: A player already has three of a tile down on the table and draws the fourth, turning their pong into a kong. If that very tile is the one you were waiting on, you take it and win instead. Only a kong made from an existing pong can be robbed.
flag.lastTile.sub: You won on the very last tile that could be drawn.
flag.lastTile.detail: The wall runs out sixteen tiles from the end. Winning on that last drawable tile scores an extra fan. It does not count if the tile came to you as a replacement after a flower or a kong.
flag.kongReplacement.sub: You konged, drew the replacement, and it won.
flag.kongReplacement.detail: After declaring a kong you draw a replacement tile from the back of the wall. If that tile completes your hand, it is worth an extra fan.
flag.flowerReplacement.sub: You drew a flower, and its replacement won.
flag.flowerReplacement.detail: Flowers, seasons and animals are set aside and replaced from the back of the wall. If the replacement completes your hand, it is worth an extra fan.
flag.heavenly.sub: You dealt, and your very first fourteen tiles already won.
flag.heavenly.detail: The dealer looks at the hand they were dealt and it is already complete, before anyone has drawn or discarded. Only the dealer can have this.
flag.earthly.sub: You won on the dealer's very first discard.
flag.earthly.detail: A non-dealer wins on the first tile the dealer throws, or on their own first draw. Only a non-dealer can have this.
flag.humanly.sub: You won in the first go round, before your first draw.
flag.humanly.detail: A non-dealer wins on a discard in the opening circuit, before drawing, with nobody having melded anything except a concealed kong.
flag.kongOnKong.sub: Two kongs in a row, and the second replacement won.
flag.kongOnKong.detail: You kong, draw the replacement, and it lets you kong again. The replacement for that second kong completes your hand. It needs at least two kongs.
flag.pao.sub: One player fed the winning hand and pays for everyone.
flag.pao.detail: Some tables play that a player who visibly hands you the hand — throwing the third dragon into two exposed dragon pongs, say — pays the whole settlement themselves and the other two pay nothing.

wizard.unusualSub: Skip this if nothing here applies.
tileinfo.jokers.singapore: Singapore mahjong does not use them. Set them aside — your count should still come to 148 without them.
tileinfo.jokers.hongkong: Hong Kong Old Style does not use them, and it has no animal tiles either. Set anything extra aside — your count should still come to 144 without them.
table.stakeHint.hongkong: What one point is worth. Hong Kong reads its money off a fixed table — three fan is 8 points, ten is 128 — so this is the dial that sets the size of the game.
table.limitHint.hongkong: The most a hand can score, {min}–{max}. Ten is the Hong Kong Mahjong Association’s limit; 8 and 13 are both played too.
table.payment: When someone throws your winning tile
table.paymentHint: Hong Kong tables play both. You collect the same either way — this only decides how the loss is shared out. Agree it before you start.
result.paymentFull: Full payment: the thrower covers the whole settlement on their own.
result.paymentHalf: Half payment: the thrower pays double and the other two pay single, so the loss is shared 2 : 1 : 1.
result.flowerNote: Seven flowers wins the hand on the spot, and it is settled as a self-draw however the tile arrived — so all three pay the same.
reject.tileNotInSet: That tile is not in this variant’s set. Take it out and try again.
reject.belowMinimum.hongkong: This hand does not reach the minimum of {min} fan, so it cannot win. Flower tiles score, but they do not count towards the minimum.
hand.notAHand: These tiles do not make a hand yet
wizard.melded: Claimed from the table — the winning tile cannot be one of these.
flag.lastTile.detail.hongkong: The wall runs out sixteen tiles from the end. Winning on that last drawable tile scores an extra fan, whether you drew it or took it off a discard. Unlike Singapore, Hong Kong still counts it when the tile came to you as a kong replacement.
flag.lastTile.sub.hongkong: You won on the very last tile of the hand.
flag.kongOnKong.detail.hongkong: You kong, draw the replacement, and it lets you kong again. The replacement for that second kong completes your hand. It needs at least two kongs, and it is worth eight fan.
flag.earthly.detail.hongkong: A non-dealer wins on the first tile the dealer throws, before anyone has claimed anything. Only a non-dealer can have this, and only off a discard.
